question: When you look up at a clear night sky, which single moment are you actually seeing?
answer: None: many moments at once. The Moon's light is 1.3 seconds old, Sirius's about 8.6 years, the Pole Star's roughly 430 years. One glance stitches together light that set out centuries apart into a picture that never existed at any single instant.
move: One view can stitch together moments that never existed side by side.
ask: Which picture I hold of a friend or a place is really a collage of different years?
reference: van Leeuwen, Validation of the new Hipparcos reduction, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 2007
